summary: Bold Monday's one-page specimen for Logical, a humanist sans whose OpenType features turn ':keywords:' and whole words into icons. The page runs on that trick: section headings end in a ':down:' arrow glyph, the hero spins an icon carousel, a typewriter types keywords that become icons, and a feature catalogue shows input → output with ID/CSS/Word how-to tooltips, all on one long turquoise-to-lime gradient.

instances.look: A full-screen turquoise gradient with 'Logical' centred in dark teal at ~160px and a yellow outline icon above it that keeps changing (⇄ arrows, fish, bottle, shield, person…)
instances.ux: The icons sit on an invisible 3D ring (translate3d around a circle) and rotate into view one at a time; no buttons
instances.learn: Spin the font's own icons on a 3D ring above the name: the hero announces the icon feature before any text explains it

reconstruction.layout: 100vh; name centred ~640px wide; icon slot ~80px above the name, centred
reconstruction.typography: Name ~160px Logical Medium, dark teal #00505a; icons ~80px from the font itself (ligatures like ':shield:'), yellow outline #f0fa00
reconstruction.behaviour: ~30 .icon divs positioned on a ring with translate3d(x, y, z); only the front one is display:inline-block; the ring steps every ~1–2s (JS)
reconstruction.assets: none (icons are glyphs of the font)

instances.look: A narrow centred paragraph in dark teal on the light turquoise gradient: 'This typeface follows a logical set of rules… a rich set of icons that are automatically transformed from words (logos in Greek)…'

reconstruction.content: Real description of the rules and icons
